name: Golf 97
tagline: A CD-ROM golf course, rendered with total sincerity
lineage: New — not yet defined anywhere but here.
story: DRAFT — a sketch to rewrite in your own words. The guess: a late-nineties sports sim on a beige tower PC. Mown stripes on the fairway, a flag that is exactly red, an interface of confident plastic bevels and Verdana, and a scorecard that takes itself completely seriously. The sky is the blue the box art promised.
principles: Bevels, not shadows: a surface is raised or sunken, never floating.
The palette is a golf course photographed at noon — grass, sand, sky, one red flag.
Chrome is beige plastic and proud of it.
Everything is labelled, like a scorecard: no icon stands alone.
do: Stripe large green surfaces like a mown fairway.
Use the red only for the flag — the single most important thing on screen.
Keep corners nearly square; this UI was drawn with rectangles.
dont: No gradients smoother than a bevel.
No dark mode; the course closes at dusk.
No irony — the style only works played straight.

voice.tone: Announcer-polite, slightly formal, delighted by par.

motion.character: Instant. Screens cut, nothing tweens — the machine had no frames to spare.

texture.notes: Mown fairway stripes, the bands a mower leaves when you look up the hole. The shadows are bevels: light from the top-left, always.

notes: DRAFT seeded as a starting point — every value here is a guess for the editor to correct, especially the story.
